title: Humanoid and Robot-Arm Manipulation in Simulation
tools: Isaac Lab · MuJoCo · PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) · Behaviour cloning · Grounding DINO · SAM 2 (Segment Anything Model 2) · Gemma 4 · OSU HPC (Oregon State University high-performance computing)
blurb: A simulated Unitree G1 humanoid walks, grasps, carries and places objects; its learned grasp picks up 345 of 360 unseen objects, up from 284.
long: My first robotics project, started in September 2026: PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) on toy tasks, then a simulated SO-101 robot arm in MuJoCo, now a Unitree G1 humanoid in NVIDIA's Isaac Lab, which simulates thousands of robots on one GPU (graphics processing unit).

Arm, from cameras only. Off-the-shelf vision models (Grounding DINO, SAM 2.1) find and outline the object, and IK (inverse kinematics) moves the arm. On 200 held-out scenes it placed 369 of 400 simple shapes and 341 of 400 household objects.
Humanoid grasp. A PPO policy controlling the waist, arm and hand lifted and held 345 of 360 unseen objects, against 284 for the previous policy. Smoothing the arm actions is what made it trainable.
Walk, carry, set down. On top of a pretrained walking network, 144 of 384 robots walked up, grasped, carried and set an object down upright.
highlights: Learned G1 humanoid grasp: 345/360 held-out objects lifted and held, vs 284 for the previous policy
Camera-only arm pick-and-place: 369/400 simple shapes, 341/400 household objects placed
Walk, grasp, carry, set down upright: 144 of 384 robots across six shapes (development runs)
Two-hand box carry learned by BC (behaviour cloning): 17/20 set down (development runs)
